purpose: Solver-level checks for the mathematical theorem and the toy mapping contract from scenario-evaluation.md.

environment.installation: z3-solver was installed into an isolated temporary --target directory; the global Python environment was not modified.

solver.name: Z3 SMT solver
solver.checksum_verification: Computed SHA-256 exactly matched the checksum published on PyPI for this wheel.

checks.purpose: Search for a counterexample to n + 0 = n over nonnegative integers.
checks.encoding: SMT integer n with constraints n >= 0 and n + 0 != n.
checks.query: exists n : Int . n >= 0 AND n + 0 != n
checks.interpretation: No counterexample exists in the encoded integer model, so the identity holds for all nonnegative integers under this encoding.

proof_object.excerpt: mp(asserted(n + 0 != n), trans(monotonicity(rewrite(n + 0 == n), n + 0 != n == n != n), rewrite(n != n == False), n + 0 != n == False), False)

checks.limitation: This is Z3's native proof object for an SMT refutation, not a theorem checked by an independently trusted proof-assistant kernel or imported into MMT.

checks.purpose: Check the declared identity mapping preserves a nonnegative integer age.
checks.interpretation: The mapping contract and its negated postcondition are inconsistent, so no counterexample exists in the encoded integer model.
checks.limitation: This validates this explicitly encoded toy contract; it does not prove arbitrary cross-formalism translations.

checks.purpose: Check division by 365 preserves the year value for exact day counts.
checks.interpretation: No counterexample exists for nonnegative integer years whose day count is exactly 365 times years, using Z3 integer division.

checks.purpose: Show that copying days directly into a years field is unsound.
checks.interpretation: A concrete counterexample exists: for one year, 365 days does not equal one year if copied without conversion.

overall_limitations: These are solver checks of explicitly encoded formulas, not DOL/MMT/SysML/Modelica conformance tests.
The arithmetic check is an SMT proof by refutation; it does not by itself produce a natural-deduction induction proof in a mathematical proof assistant.
The mapping tests establish only the stated integer constraints, not full semantics for identity, units, uncertainty, provenance, or empirical grounding.
No canonical, minimal, or MECE factorization is established by these checks.
